official.deadline_note: The scheme pages published on the High Commission of India, Dhaka portal listed 30 April 2025 as the last date for A.Y. 2025-26; the ICCR A2A portal now shows Registration Year: 2026-27, but no published closing date for the 2026-27 round was found on the official pages checked.
official.application_cycle: ICCR Scholarship Programme 2026-27 (A2A portal Registration Year: 2026-27)
official.status_note: No open or closed statement for the 2026-27 round appears on the official pages checked; the ICCR site lists the Suborno Jayanti Scholarship Scheme for Bangladesh nationals with 500 slots under the 2026-27 programme.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Facilities listed for the scheme: 'Tuition fee/OCF paid to Universities (Norms attached)'.
benefits: Facilities listed by ICCR for the scheme: Stipend, HRA, Contingent Allowances, Thesis/Dissertation Allowance, Airfare, Tuition fee/OCF paid to Universities (Norms attached)
Financial terms: Stipend (per month, from the date of joining of the Institute on pro-rata basis): Undergraduate 18,000, Postgraduate 20,000, M.Phil/Ph.D 22,000
House Rent Allowance (per month, along with monthly stipend): 6,500 in Grade 1 cities, 5,500 in other cities
Contingent Grant (per annum): Undergraduate 5,000, Postgraduate (admitted in A.Y. 2023-24 & onwards) 7,000, Ph.D 12,500
Thesis and Dissertation Expenses (once in the entire duration of the course): Ph.D scholar 10,000; 7,000 for all other courses where a project report is required to be submitted
Medical Insurance Policy has to be procured by students with minimum sum assured of INR 5 00,000 per annum - a mandatory requirement for availing ICCR Scholarships
Stipend and HRA are payable to the students from the date of joining the institution
eligibility: Suborno Jayanti Scholarship Scheme: 500 slots for nationals of Bangladesh for UG, PG and Ph.D. courses in universities of India (ICCR-funding scheme of 2026-27)
Levels offered: UG, PG, Ph.D.; streams: STEM & Non-STEM (50% each)
Prohibited courses/streams: Medical, Law, and Integrated
coverage: Tuition fee/OCF paid to universities (norms attached)
Monthly stipend by level (UG INR 18,000, PG INR 20,000, PhD INR 22,000)
House Rent Allowance per month (INR 6,500 Grade 1 cities, INR 5,500 other cities)
Contingent grant per year and one-time thesis/dissertation allowance
Return economy class airfare to the airport nearest to the place of study and 3-tier AC train fare if required to the place of study in India
Medical insurance with minimum INR 5,00,000 sum assured (mandatory)
application_method: Schemes and slot allocations for 2026-27 are published on the ICCR website; ICCR links applicants to its online scholarship portal (a2ascholarships.iccr.gov.in) to apply
official.application_route: Apply through the ICCR online portal (a2ascholarships.iccr.gov.in); Bangladesh applicants follow the Suborno Jayanti scheme pages published on the High Commission of India, Dhaka portal (sjsdhaka.gov.in).
official.citizenship_residency: Bangladesh nationals (one country covered by the scheme)
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the scheme is an outbound award for Bangladeshi nationals studying in India
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: All programmes offered by universities excluding Medical, Law and Integrated; streams split 50% STEM and 50% non-STEM
official.description: The Suborno Jayanti Scholarship Scheme offers 500 scholarships annually under the ICCR Scholarship Programme 2026-27 to nationals of Bangladesh for UG, PG and Ph.D. studies in universities of India, with stipend, HRA, contingent and thesis allowances, airfare and tuition/OCF paid to universities; Medical, Law and Integrated programmes are prohibited.
official.program_type: ICCR scholarship scheme (Suborno Jayanti Scholarship Scheme) under the ICCR Scholarship Programme 2026-27

not_confirmed: documents required and selection criteria (not listed in the scheme table on the ICCR schemes page)
verification.notes: Scheme structure, slots, prohibited courses and benefit categories from the ICCR schemes page; stipend/HRA/contingent/thesis rates from the official ICCR Financial Terms for the A.Y. 2025-26 published on the High Commission of India, Dhaka portal. This corrects the catalogue: HRA is city-grade based (INR 6,500/5,500), not level-based, and the UG contingent grant is INR 5,000 (not 5,500), with a separate PhD thesis allowance of INR 10,000.

applicant_utility.summary: If you are a Bangladeshi national with an Indian degree in mind, this scheme pays tuition and other charges directly to the university, adds a monthly stipend of INR 18,000-22,000 depending on your level, a city-grade based house rent allowance, a yearly contingent grant and return economy airfare once your programme runs a year or more. Your own budget must still cover hostel and mess charges, security deposit and caution money, certificate and immigration-related fees, and any charge outside ICCR norms, because the official 'charges payable by the student' list is explicit. Medicine, law and integrated courses are excluded outright, so confirm your intended degree is eligible before you spend money preparing documents.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Bangladeshi school and college leavers and recent graduates from households that cannot fund a full Indian degree abroad without state support.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your intended programme is not medical, law or integrated, and that your stream matches the 50/50 STEM and non-STEM split of the scheme
Prepare for mandatory medical insurance with a minimum sum assured of INR 5,00,000, which the financial terms make a condition
Track the A2A portal (a2ascholarships.iccr.gov.in) for the current registration year rather than relying on last year's cycle dates
Budget separately for hostel or mess, security deposit and caution money, and for the initial air ticket that ICCR reimburses as return economy airfare
common_rejection_risks: Applying for a prohibited course - Medical, Law and Integrated programmes are not funded under the scheme
Assuming the stipend repeats exactly at every level: the rate steps from UG INR 18,000 to PG INR 20,000 to PhD INR 22,000 and HRA depends on the city grade, not your degree
Applying late in the annual window: the published A.Y. 2025-26 last date was 30 April, and windows close on the embassy/portal calendar
Forgetting the mandatory INR 5,00,000 medical insurance requirement stated in the official financial terms
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Hostel or private accommodation and mess charges, security deposit and caution money, fees for obtaining certificates, registration/penalty fees for immigration compliance, any other fees or charges not covered under scholarship norms, and charges for non-compulsory subjects.
document_audit: The ICCR schemes page itself does not publish a document checklist, so rely on the ICCR guidelines PDFs published on the High Commission of India, Dhaka portal before assembling anything
Keep proof ready of which city grade your host institution falls in, because the HRA rate depends on it (INR 6,500 vs 5,500)
Retain evidence of the insurance policy meeting the INR 5,00,000 minimum sum assured, since it is mandatory rather than optional
alerts: Amounts quoted come from the official A.Y. 2025-26 financial terms; the ICCR page notes that norms are attached and can be revised for the 2026-27 round
Airfare is return economy class to the airport nearest to the place of study plus 3-tier AC train fare only if required
Applications for the scheme run through the annual cycle, so the A2A portal registration year is the thing to watch, not the calendar year
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Watch the ICCR A2A portal and the Suborno Jayanti scheme pages for the registration window, apply online before the published last date, and then track selection and document follow-up through the portal and the High Commission of India, Dhaka channel.

official.deadline_note: Deadlines are set per programme: the DAAD FAQ directs applicants to the 'Application procedure' tab of each Call for Applications in the scholarship database; no single central closing date is published.
official.application_cycle: Per-programme application windows published in the DAAD scholarship database
official.status_note: DAAD programmes run on their own calendars; the DAAD Bangladesh site (Information Centre Dhaka) posts current calls, e.g. the HSK 2026-2027 university summer course call announced on 17 September 2026.
official.tuition_coverage_note: 'DAAD does not pay tuition fees for its scholarship holders' - the FAQ notes Baden-Württemberg charges EUR 1,500 per semester for international students from non-EU/EEA countries and TUM EUR 4,000-6,000 per semester for master's programmes from winter semester 2024/2025.
benefits: Scholars taking a Master's programme typically receive EUR 992 a month; doctoral candidates and postdocs EUR 1,400
Rates for university teachers are usually EUR 2,000 for assistant teachers, assistant professors and lecturers and EUR 2,150 for professors
Lump-sum allowance towards travel expenses, with a top-up in some programmes for bus or train travel
Partner allowance of EUR 276 a month and child allowance of EUR 259 a month per child where there is no state child benefit entitlement (for funding periods over six months)
In many scholarship programmes insurance benefits are included: the DAAD takes out private health insurance and pays the premiums
Additional benefits for people with a disability or chronic illness can be applied for after selection and are granted case by case
eligibility: No fixed age limit usually; some programmes require that only a certain amount of time should have elapsed since the last degree
Applicants already in Germany are eligible if they have been there a maximum of 15 months by the closing date

Applying outside the country of origin: for stays longer than 6 months the last degree must have been obtained in the country of residence (or be obtained by the start of the scholarship); short-term stays need one year of residence
Full-time study or research with compulsory attendance in Germany; distance, blended, part-time and dual programmes are not eligible
A full DAAD scholarship is not compatible with Erasmus funding, and simultaneous funding by another German state agency is excluded
Scholarships with a funding period of at least 7 months cannot be combined within one educational period; research grants are possible once per educational period
requirements: Proof of current proficiency in the language of instruction (German, English or both) as listed in the Call for Applications; language certificates should not be older than 3 years

For university admission you must also submit the university's required language proof (e.g. DSH or TestDaF for German-taught, TOEFL or IELTS for English-taught programmes; level C1 is often required)
Applications can be submitted in German or English unless the Call states otherwise; documents in other languages must be translated, and translations need not be certified
Research proposals (max 10 pages) with a separate time plan upload, and letters of recommendation by university teachers with a doctoral degree for the relevant programme
documents: Online application in the DAAD portal with all documents listed in the Call for Applications (artistic work samples go via a media database)
Letter confirming academic supervision from the German host for individual research or a doctorate, including confirmation of a workplace and the working language
Motivation letter of 1-3 pages for study scholarships; research proposal of max 10 pages with the time plan as a separate document
University certificates and transcripts (certified versions only after a positive selection decision)
selection_criteria: Professional qualification: academic achievements, grade development, academic progress, language skills, internships and work experience
Quality of the study or research project and its preparation (choice of programme/host, contacts, feasibility and consistency of the plan and schedule)
Potential of the applicant: motivation, prospects for further academic, professional and personal development, and extracurricular commitment

Special circumstances - disability, chronic or prolonged illness, raising children, caring for relatives, extensive employment to finance studies, refugee background - are compensated in the assessment
Independent voluntary selection committees decide; DAAD staff have no vote and the best applicants may be invited to a personal interview
coverage: Monthly scholarship paid according to academic level and programme
Lump-sum travel allowance, with a top-up in some programmes for bus or train travel
Insurance benefits in many programmes, including the private health insurance premiums
Partner and child allowances where the programme provides for family members (funding over six months)
Tuition fees are NOT paid by DAAD
application_method: Read the 'Application procedure' section of the Call for Applications in the scholarship database (funding-guide.de)
Where indicated, apply online via the DAAD portal ('Submit application' tab, visible during an open application period)
Get advice from the contact persons listed under 'Contact and advice' - in Bangladesh, the DAAD Information Centre in Dhaka
official.application_route: Choose the programme in the DAAD scholarship database and follow that Call's procedure - usually the DAAD portal - and use the DAAD Information Centre Dhaka for advice on the shortlist.
official.study_mode: Full-time study or research with compulsory attendance in Germany; distance, blended, part-time and dual programmes are not eligible
official.citizenship_residency: Apply from your country of origin; dual nationals apply from the country where they have spent most of their life, and applying from two countries at the same time is not allowed
official.international_eligibility: Yes - DAAD funds international students and researchers; the DAAD Information Centre in Dhaka is the point of contact for Bangladesh
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Programmes are open to almost all subjects although restrictions apply to some subjects (e.g. medicine); some programmes target specific areas such as architecture, music or computer science
official.research_requirement: For individual research or a doctorate, a letter confirming academic supervision in Germany; research grants require a detailed proposal (max 10 pages) plus a separate time plan
official.description: The DAAD (German Academic Exchange Service) runs a database of scholarship programmes for study, research and teaching in Germany: monthly stipends by academic level, a lump-sum travel allowance and, in many programmes, insurance and family benefits - but DAAD does not pay tuition fees.
official.program_type: Database of DAAD scholarship programmes (study, research and teaching in Germany)
official.english_requirement: Proof of current proficiency in the language of instruction; for English-taught programmes the FAQ lists IELTS, TOEFL iBT/Essentials, TOEIC, Cambridge, PTE Academic, Duolingo English Test and others as acceptable evidence (university admission requirements may differ; certificates not older than 3 years)

verification.notes: Stipend rates and family/travel/insurance benefits from the DAAD 'Important information for scholarship applicants' FAQ (Section F); the doctoral/postdoc monthly rate is now EUR 1,400, so the catalogue's EUR 1,300 is out of date; the FAQ states DAAD does not pay tuition fees, so fully_funded is false.

applicant_utility.summary: DAAD is a database rather than one scholarship, so your first job is finding the programme that matches your level and subject and then reading that Call's own deadline and document list. Expect EUR 992 a month as a master's student, EUR 1,400 as a doctoral candidate or postdoc, a lump-sum travel allowance and in many programmes DAAD-arranged health insurance - but plan for tuition yourself, because DAAD does not pay university fees and places like Baden-Württemberg (EUR 1,500 per semester) or TUM (EUR 4,000-6,000 per semester) charge them. Winning the scholarship is still not admission: you must secure your own place at a German university or the award is forfeited.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Self-directed graduates and doctoral candidates with strong grades and a convincing project story who can manage several separate application calendars at once.
application_readiness_checklist: Shortlist programmes in the DAAD scholarship database by level, subject and country, and read each Call's 'Application procedure' and 'Application documents' tabs before drafting
Check two language requirements: what the scholarship asks for (proof of the language of instruction) and separately what your chosen university's admission requires (often C1)
For research or a doctorate, secure a German supervisor first and get the informal letter confirming supervision, a workplace and the working language
Send your shortlist and timing plan to the DAAD Information Centre in Dhaka - it is the official local contact point for Bangladesh
If you have been in Germany, count your months: more than 15 months by the closing date normally makes you ineligible
common_rejection_risks: Assuming one DAAD deadline - each programme closes on its own date and several are annual
Missing the language-of-instruction proof, or submitting a certificate older than 3 years
Holding a full Erasmus grant or another German state-agency scholarship, which blocks simultaneous DAAD funding
A weak research proposal or motivation letter: the committees score project preparation, feasibility and consistency of the schedule explicitly
Budgeting only for the stipend and then discovering the chosen university charges tuition
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: University tuition fees where charged (non-EU/EEA international students in Baden-Württemberg: EUR 1,500 per semester; TUM master's: EUR 4,000-6,000 per semester from winter semester 2024/2025; private universities and non-consecutive programmes can charge more), plus the gap between the stipend and high city rents that the DAAD FAQ itself warns about.
document_audit: Certificates and transcripts do not need to be certified at application - only after a positive selection decision - but keep originals retrievable
Documents in other languages must be translated into German or English; the translation need not be certified and you may translate yourself
The research proposal has a 10-page maximum and the time plan must be uploaded as a separate file
If AI tools are used in preparing the application, the DAAD requires an explicit note in the documents ('Produced with the aid of the tool used')
alerts: A full DAAD scholarship is not compatible with Erasmus funding
Scholarship without admission means the funding is forfeited, so apply to several universities early

Health insurance is compulsory from day one; the DAAD-arranged insurance excludes pre-existing conditions such as HIV, multiple sclerosis, haemophilia, cancer including leukaemia and chronic kidney disease, and births within 8 months of cover
Any part-time income above EUR 603 gross per month, or a second scholarship, is deducted from the DAAD payment
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Select the programme in the database, apply inside its window (usually via the DAAD portal with all listed documents), wait on the independent selection committee decision, then arrange university admission and insurance separately.
